answer: Each identity claims one garden plot on karst and registers its drainage response kernel: verifiers order a live test, place a coded marker, pour 200 litres at a random corner, and log sink time and spring outflow. That curve is a physical fingerprint no other plot reproduces, and replays mismatch weather records. Faking 1,000 identities needs 1,000 surveyed plots at $380 each plus leases and an operator within 1 hour of each random test; a missed or cloned curve revokes the slot. Trade-off: heavy rain widens error bands, so tests pause in storms and admission slows.
